candidates.unit: Typed, pure backend revision/transition receipt preparation
candidates.problem: Live append and administrative append independently assemble the same linked revision/receipt pair, hash the same request input, and validate the same body/state/operation relation. Any future new receipt field or hash binding must currently be updated twice. Separate SQL writers do not require separate pair construction.
candidates.manualDuplicate: Both sequences set revision = previous revision + 1, previousId, lastReceiptId, creation time, then validateBody -> assertBackendTransition -> validateTransition, then sign a receipt linking before/after IDs, after SHA, request ID, request SHA and immutable request input. This is a repeated value construction sequence, not a claim that the whole functions are equivalent.
fix: Add a private typed preparation function taking the already-selected kind/entity/workspace, before/body, normalized request input, revision ID, receipt ID, operation and timestamp. It returns the immutable signed record/receipt pair. Keep this function free of DatabaseSync, transaction creation, ports, caches, randomUUID and current time.

Preserve the current signing and validation order and the existing immutableKnowledgeJson/knowledgeHash implementation and limits. Caller-specific body/state/request selection remains outside the helper.

Use the preparation function from live append and appendAdministrative only after their current row/quota checks and ID/time capture. Preserve the first-create previousId/null behavior and administrative prior revision behavior.
delete: Remove only the two duplicated revision/receipt assembly sequences once replaced. Do not delete either caller, Original port, domain validator, operation state branch or SQL failure path.
add: One internal record/receipt input/output type and preparation function in this domain, optionally a short internal source file if it improves bounded responsibility. No new public export, service framework or general JSON parser.

A regression exercising independently read native SQL rows and independent archive validation for a live transition plus recover and pause-import transitions, with immutable request inputs and deterministic captured IDs/timestamps.
retain: Live expectedRevision check, per-kind first-create limits, total revision row/byte limits and historical request dedupe before Original producer reads/current CAS.

Caller-owned sync writeTx, both row insert statements, conditional initial head INSERT versus previous ID/revision/SHA UPDATE, changes === 1 checks and transaction rollback. Do not move writes or acquire a new/nested transaction in the preparation helper.

UUID and timestamp creation at their present points: live time() validation after quota checks; administrative timestamp supplied by recovery/import. Preserve recovery/import request ID formats and archive SHA binding.

Recovery remains uncertain/owner-lost; import remains paused-import/disabled and imported. Never recreate an Original handle, dispatch a request, upgrade unknown to success, retry a prior effect or invent cleanup evidence.

Original owner/connection/tool/completion/read permission capture, descriptor/proxy rejection, dispatch-versus-observe differences and all per-operation transition validation. Keep backendRecords single original instance and any outer store evidence/cache ownership.

Independent validateAgentBackendDatabase/validateOwnerSql checks and archive traversal stay separate from writer construction. Their independent SQL-column/hash/transition comparisons must not reuse a writer-derived expected graph.

Writer column projection stays local initially: live connection column uses eid for connection kind; administrative column uses after.connectionId. Validate rather than silently normalize any disagreement.
Backend payload header-before-read 65,536-byte bound versus native primary row 262,144-byte bound, depth/node/identifier/error distinctions and import workspace scoping remain unchanged.
candidates.publicBoundary: Engine exports backend record/input types, while SqliteStore and direct domain imports consume AgentBackendStorage and recovery/import functions. Keep every existing signature and serialized field; no value-export removal is justified by AST call counts.

gates: Run focused source/native SQLite tests after implementation; retain real head-CAS fault rollback with no orphan revision/receipt and dedupe with zero new Original reads.

Compare resulting native columns and canonical record/receipt JSON under fixed UUID/time captures; separately assert headers, receipt scopes, request SHA, after SHA and graph validity without using the new builder as the expected-value generator.

Use genuine completed and cancelled history export/import/recovery scenarios: preserve historical IDs; only required administrative revisions appear; disabled/paused/unknown states and quarantine remain; no provider/process recreation or replay.
Run engine source typecheck and Root-owned compiled/full regression at the agreed integration boundary.

candidates.rollback: Implement as one isolated reversible source change; keep original callers and schema. If serialization/error order, native SQL fault behavior, archive verification or Original ownership differs, revert the helper replacement. No migration/data rewrite is involved.
candidates.limitation: Not a rewrite of the high-complexity validateBody/validateTransition validators. Their branches encode operation-specific proof semantics and require a separate operation matrix before any reduction.

candidates.unit: One private predicate for the exact live tool-owner checks shared by team and workflow
candidates.problem: The two methods authenticate the same captured original ToolContext using the same 14 owner/signal/binding/native Turn/Attempt/tool state comparisons in the same order. Drift between these predicates could admit one lane after the other rejects an expired execution. Domain-specific allowlists, approvals and errors remain separate.
candidates.manualDuplicate: After capture/phase/active and plain-data binding checks, team and workflow each compare owners-map identity, owner terminal/abort, original signal identity/abort, binding, active tool object identity, Run session/ID/workspace, Turn/Attempt IDs, tool ID and requested-versus-running state. Their allowlist is tested first. Team and workflow have identical internal ordering; readonly command job has a related predicate but checks Run ID before Session ID.
fix: Add a private boolean predicate receiving the already-authenticated capture, original context, phase and binding. Extract only the identical 14-condition block from team and workflow, preserving short-circuit field order.

Keep each method's WeakMap lookup, phase/active check, binding guard and errors in their current order. Keep the allowlist on the left of the helper call so an unsupported name does not trigger extra owner/context reads.

Keep current catalogue/discovery verification and the separate allowed approval/fingerprint/session/Run/tool/name checks at the same points in each wrapper. Preserve every existing error code/message, including the current TEAM_MODEL_OWNER_STALE error from teamContextBinding for all consumers.
delete: Remove the duplicated team/workflow owner comparison block only. Do not delete wrapper methods, names, tool registry entries, captures or approval checks.
add: A private capture type if necessary to express the existing WeakMap value once; no public type/API change.

Parameterize meaningful native-context negative scenarios across actual team and workflow operations: copied object, accessor/proxy, stale original signal, original owner/active-tool/Turn/Attempt drift and replaced approval. Assert zero effect and zero getter/proxy invocation where applicable, as well as the existing lane error.
retain: The actual toolOperation capture uses the exact WeakMap key and remains active only during that original prepare/execute operation. Identical serialized tuples cannot become Original authority.

Team allowlist and its read_mailbox/read_board execute approval exemption; workflow allowlist and observe_workflow_stage exemption. Exact native approval remains mandatory for each respective mutation.
Readonly command job guard stays unchanged in this initial unit because its Run ID/Session ID evaluation order differs; its source/budget proof and return catalogue/profile fields remain local.

Code mode uses a separate WeakMap and observe phase that intentionally permits bounded cleanup/observation after abort. Owned-command start/settle uses a separate WeakMap and settle can consume cleanup after abort. Do not route either through a live non-aborted predicate.
Dynamic native tool registration, option gates, exactApproval policy, tool catalogue/discovery capture, nested operation signals/timeouts and final inProgress=false cleanup.
Public RunCoordinator class/method signatures and direct host dependencies; no AST-based method export removal or new authorization framework.

gates: Exercise actual dynamically registered team and workflow mutation/read tools through both prepare and execute; verify catalogue capture happens only after original owner checks and actual approvals still bind exact native rows.

Run accessor/proxy/copied-owner cases with zero effect/trap assertions; add a workflow equivalent if the existing suite does not cover that exact original-context lane. Reject phase mismatch, inactive original operation and stale native Turn/Attempt with the same errors.
Retain readonly job positive/negative controls unchanged. Separately run code-mode post-abort observe and owned-command settle/close tests to detect an accidental expansion of the live predicate.
Run provider cleanup, cancellation and coordinator close tests with Original handles, plus Root-owned compiled/full regression. No historical PID signaling or replay is introduced.

candidates.rollback: Keep wrapper methods and private captures intact. Revert the one predicate extraction if field evaluation order, error precedence, approval timing, dynamic tool behavior or post-abort cleanup changes. No durable data change is involved.
candidates.limitation: This bounded two-caller extraction does not resolve the larger provider/client effect or executeTool responsibilities; their different timeout, approval, native effect and cleanup paths need independent semantic work.

retainReviewedOwners.decision: Retain durable queued acceptance versus v1 immediate/busy receipts, workspace FIFO/session flights, beforePromotion callbacks, bounded steer cutoff, recovery quarantine and close/join. The two promotion sites operate on distinct accepted inputs versus steer batches; combining them would hide rather than remove stateful responsibility.

Retain graph/transition/column validation independence and payload-before-decode bounds. High syntax complexity alone does not justify deleting proof cases or combining domain parsers with different limits/errors.
Retain different Original signal/approval/source ownership and post-abort observe/settle obligations. Preserve unknown outcomes and noReplay behavior.
No deletion candidate is approved. Keep exported methods/types, source-level consumers, archive validators and frozen v1 behavior until consumer evidence and functional tests prove removal safe.

limits: Audit covers three measured production modules and listed caller/test sources. It is not a repository-wide security audit, full semantic unused-code analysis or final all-owned baseline.

Tests above were inspected as evidence and are required future gates; no test/build/live/native process/provider/database operation was run for these proposals. Previous CI/engine results belong to their separately pinned investigations.

No claim of reduced lines/complexity or completed RF01/RF02 is made before implementation and a final source-pinned measurement. Reject a helper that merely relocates the two functions without removing their repeated value construction or exact predicate responsibility.
Concurrent feature integration can invalidate these pins. Verify pins and refresh affected source/AST/caller evidence before implementation; Root owns the final baseline and TODO rewrite.
